themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls are about meaning and worth, not data: whether a picture plus a headline implies a promise, whether the evidence really backs a claim, what the word customer means, what one more message is worth. No formula settles these, because the disagreement usually has budget attached.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance all three models said the real blocker is implied or emergent meaning that no checker sees, and the same shape appears in the fights over what customer means in the semantic context layer problem and in the missing price of a message in cross-channel journey orchestration.

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it. So the models start small: label the cases you can already prove, run a fixed panel of buyer questions, or leave a holdout running forever just to have something honest to grade against.
themes.evidence: Answer engine optimization has no stable baseline because answers shift run to run, incrementality measurement is chased by platforms that re-optimize against the test, identity resolution has no truth set about who is the same person, and content governance work starts by mining past reviewer rejections for labels.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Safe agent execution answers converge on a single proxy or gateway with hard spend and audience caps, downstream consent work starts by forcing all data exits through one gate, and content governance answers restrict the model to assembling pre-approved claims rather than checking freeform copy afterward.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, a dollar, or a piece of content leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. The best anyone offers is watching from outside: planting fake records, expiring every list you send, or judging results only by outcomes you can see yourself.
themes.evidence: Downstream consent and deletion answers agree that a person cannot be untrained out of a model and that walled gardens will not let you read back, ad supply integrity answers fall back on judging spend against your own sales records, and agent execution answers note vendors expose no rollback.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the party who holds the answer gains nothing by handing it over, and nobody can make them. So the models try to make honesty pay better than hiding, or they stop waiting for cooperation and work only with what they already own.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers propose fast lanes and discounts so declaring beats pretending to be a browser, journey orchestration answers say channel owners will subvert coordination that cuts their credited numbers, and identity resolution answers point to platform owners who profit from keeping identity fragmented.
